title: CapitalTrust Bank — Data Residency & Compliance Discovery
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
summary: Initial discovery on regulatory and residency requirements. CapitalTrust is exploring Redwood's Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options to determine whether data can remain in EU/US regions, how logging and audit logs are handled, and what controls are needed for finance/HIPAA-adjacent workloads. Action: Redwood to send SOC2, ISO artifacts, data residency matrix, and propose a technical deep dive and a short pilot scope.
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC 2 + ISO27001 summary and data residency matrix (Lena)
Schedule technical deep dive with infra team to review VPC/private deployment options and key management (Rahul)
Customer to confirm internal stakeholders for procurement and legal (Marcus)
Agree on pilot success criteria and timeline — propose 4-week pilot (Talia)
Share preliminary pricing for Dedicated and Private options (Lena)

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-09-15
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Rahul Mehra (Redwood SE), Talia Gomez (Redwood CSM), Dana Liu (CapitalTrust Head of Security), Marcus Chen (CTO), Jared O'Neil (Product), Samantha Reyes (Legal)

Summary (auto): High-level compliance and residency requirements; initial fit for Dedicated vs Private; request for artifacts and tech deep dive.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Lena, I'm the AE on this account, with Rahul our solutions engineer, and Talia from customer success. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Marcus Chen: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to get this kicked off.
[00:09] Dana Liu: Hi, thanks. Dana here — head of security at CapitalTrust. We want to make sure any LLM infra meets our regional controls.
[00:14] Lena Park: Great, thanks Dana. The purpose of today's call is to understand your residency, logging, and compliance constraints so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Rahul will jump into the technical bits when needed.
[00:24] Rahul Mehra: Hi all. I'll mostly listen then cover tech details — VPC, KMS, logging, and fallback policies.
[00:29] Jared O'Neil: Quick context: product wants to use Redwood for a customer support assistant that will occasionally surface account info and transaction metadata. Primary concerns: PII handling, retention, and keeping EU customer data in EU.
[00:41] Samantha Reyes: From legal, we need to know data processor arrangements, subprocessors list, and whether logs containing identifiers can be purged or masked.
[00:49] Lena Park: Totally. Can you walk us through current stack? Where do you host customer data today and what's your identity setup?
[00:55] Marcus Chen: We run services in AWS, multiple accounts. EU customers are in eu-west-1. We use Okta for SSO, KMS for key management, and some HSM for critical workloads. We currently self-host some models for inference for highly sensitive flows.
[01:08] Dana Liu: Compliance-wise: GDPR for EU customers, PCI for payment data (we tokenize at rest), and we have some HIPAA-adjacent processes for certain partner integrations. We're cautious about sending raw PII out-of-region.
[01:19] Rahul Mehra: Sounds familiar. Redwood Hosted API can be region-restricted but hosted TOS may involve subprocessors — we have a dedicated offer (Redwood Dedicated) where we reserve GPU pools, and Private which can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem. Each has different controls around logs and KMS.
[01:33] Jared O'Neil: Can we keep EU-customer requests entirely in eu region using Hosted?
[01:37] Lena Park: With Hosted, you can route requests to EU regions but you should check the subprocessors and data residency guarantees — hosted typically stores metadata and logs in our control plane; we can provide a data residency matrix. For strict residency, Dedicated or Private is safer.
[01:49] Dana Liu: What about logs — access logs, request/response retention. We need audit logs for 7 years and ability to redact PII from logs on demand.
[02:00] Rahul Mehra: On Dedicated, logs can be isolated; you control retention windows in many cases, and we can integrate with your SIEM. For Private, logs stay in your VPC and you control retention entirely. For Hosted, we offer configurable retention but some audit logs for platform operations may be retained per our policy. We'll send the exact retention options.
[02:17] Samantha Reyes: Also need to know about encryption at rest and in transit, and whether we can bring our own keys (BYOK).
[02:24] Rahul Mehra: BYOK is supported for Private deployments and on Dedicated via KMS integration; HSM-level controls are possible on Private/on-prem. Hosted supports managed keys; we have KMS integrations with customer-managed keys for certain enterprise contracts.
[02:36] Marcus Chen: Ok that's helpful. Any certification artifacts? SOC2, ISO, penetration test reports?
[02:41] Lena Park: Yes, we can share SOC2 Type II summary and ISO27001 certificate. We'll redact where needed for public sharing but can provide more under NDA.
[02:50] Marcus Chen: And subprocessors list? We need to do DPIA (data protection impact assessment) for GDPR.
[02:56] Lena Park: We'll include subprocessors list and data processor agreement template.
[03:00] Dana Liu: About PII in model inputs — do you do any deterministic redaction or tokenization before sending to model? For Hosted we need guarantee that raw identifiers don't get stored in logs.
[03:10] Rahul Mehra: We offer prefix/KV caching and configurable redaction pipelines; for Hosted we can configure masking on the platform but the safest is to do client-side redaction or use Dedicated/Private so log pipelines are under your control. We'll go into detail in the tech deep dive.
[03:24] Jared O'Neil: Any limitations on throughput or latency when using Private/VPC? Our SLA for support assistant is sub-200ms for common requests.
[03:32] Rahul Mehra: Latency depends on instance types and model choice; Dedicated is tuned for predictable throughput with GPU pools and autoscaling, Private can match that but requires sizing. We can run benchmarks during a pilot — we have example configs that hit sub-200ms for certain models with batching. We'll propose a benchmarking plan.
[03:48] Samantha Reyes: HIPAA — we have a partner that routes certain health-adjacent data; we need to confirm Business Associate Agreement (BAA) viability.
[03:56] Lena Park: Redwood offers BAAs for customers with HIPAA needs on certain deployment types — typically Dedicated or Private. We'll flag legal to follow up.
[04:05] Marcus Chen: Cost question — Dedicated vs Private cost profiles?
[04:09] Lena Park: Dedicated is a reserved capacity model with monthly commits — predictable unit costs. Private includes platform licensing plus infra; often higher fixed cost but gives maximum control. We'll share a pricing sketch.
[04:21] Dana Liu: One more: audit logs — we need immutable logs with WORM for some flows. Is that something Redwood can provide?
[04:29] Rahul Mehra: For Private, you can configure WORM via your storage. For Dedicated we can enable write-once policies in collaboration; Hosted is limited by our platform capabilities.
[04:39] Jared O'Neil: Great. Can we get a sample of the logging schema so our engineers can evaluate PII fields?
[04:45] Rahul Mehra: Yes — we'll include logging schema and examples, with notes on how to redact or mask fields.
[04:50] Lena Park: To recap next steps: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, subprocessors list, data residency matrix, logging schema, and propose a technical deep dive and a 4-week pilot with benchmarks.
[04:59] Marcus Chen: Sounds good. We'll gather stakeholders and get back on availability for the deep dive.
[05:04] Samantha Reyes: I'll review legal constraints and send anything that blocks subprocessors.
[05:08] Lena Park: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with artifacts and a calendar invite.
[05:12] Dana Liu: Thanks all.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words, proper nouns may be slightly off (e.g., Okta typed as "Octa" in places), and some timestamps are approximate.

Action Items (as recorded):
- Lena to send security artifacts and data residency matrix.
- Rahul to prep tech deep dive covering VPC, KMS, logging retention, and benchmarking plan.
- Marcus to confirm stakeholders.
- Samantha to surface any legal showstoppers.
